title: 1961 AHSME Problem 34
statement: Let \(S\) be the set of values assumed by the fraction \[ \frac{2x+3}{x+2} \] when \(x\) is any member of the interval \(x\ge0.\) Let \(M\) be the least upper bound of \(S,\) and let \(m\) be the greatest lower bound of \(S.\) We may then say:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
\(m\) is in \(S,\) but \(M\) is not in
\(S\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: \(M\) is in \(S,\) but \(m\) is not in \(S\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: \(M\) does not exist either in or outside \(S\)

solutions.text:
We have \[ \frac{2x+3}{x+2}=2-\frac1{x+2}. \] For \(x\ge0,\) this increases from \(\frac{3}{2}\) toward \(2\) without reaching \(2.\) Thus \(S=[\frac32,2),\) so its greatest lower bound \(m=\frac{3}{2}\) belongs to \(S,\) while its least upper bound \(M=2\) does not.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Evaluate the lower endpoint and examine the limit as \(x\) increases
